title: Where it grows
subtitle: Piedmont's hills
objectives: Explain its place in Piedmont's vineyards

steps.title: Piedmont
steps.body: Dolcetto grows almost only in Piedmont and nearby Liguria, where it's called Ormeasco. Main zones are Alba, Dogliani, Ovada and Diano d'Alba. Because it ripens early, growers plant it on cooler, higher or north-facing slopes, leaving the warmest sites for Nebbiolo.

steps.title: DOCGs
steps.body: Three Dolcetto zones are DOCG: Dogliani, Diano d'Alba and Ovada Superiore. Dogliani, south of Barolo, is considered its spiritual home, where Dolcetto is the main grape rather than a sideline. Dogliani wines are fuller and can age a little more.

steps.explanation: Dolcetto fills the cooler sites of Piedmont.

steps.body: In Piedmont, Dolcetto has lost ground to Barbera and Nebbiolo, which fetch higher prices. A good Dolcetto d'Alba or Dogliani is often a bargain.

steps.prompt: Why is Dolcetto planted on cooler slopes?
steps.explanation: Early ripening means it doesn't need the warmest sites.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Dolcetto grows in Piedmont, mainly Alba, Dogliani and Ovada
It takes cooler slopes, leaving warm ones for Nebbiolo
Dogliani is its spiritual home and a DOCG
